After lunch, information on crate labels
This article helps

Crate labels and supporting papers

At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps crate labels consistent so each animal can be matched with the right booking and handled with care. The label should stay clean, secure, and easy to read from the outside of the crate. If a label is loose, faded, or covered by tape, replace it before the animal is accepted for travel.

The welfare coordinator checks that the label shows the key comfort details needed by crews. These details help us guide the animal through the journey and reduce avoidable stress during handling. The passenger coordinator then confirms that the travel steps are complete and that the crate information matches the booking record. When both checks are done, the file moves forward without delay.

Use clear plain text on every label. Keep the animal name, owner name, and route details aligned with the approved travel papers. If a traveler arrives with a handwritten label, review it for legibility before approval. If the crate is shared with supplies, remove unrelated notes so only travel information remains visible.

Crew members rely on the label to know how to position the crate and how to treat the animal during transfer. The department also shares practical instructions with ground staff so the same standards are used at each handoff. A label that is complete and readable supports a smooth process from desk review to loading.

If a traveler reports a problem, stay calm and check the record before making changes. Explain which item is missing or unclear, then ask for the corrected document or label. If a pet such as Milo is in transit, keep the focus on comfort, identification, and clear communication until the file is ready.

When in doubt, review the booking notes, confirm the label against the papers, and escalate any mismatch to the senior coordinator. For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways.
